**Eq. 5 (page 3):**

$$L_3(\mathcal{C}) = L_2(\mathcal{C}) + \lambda \cdot L_1(\mathcal{C})$$

The terms are defined as follows:

- **$L_2(\mathcal{C})$** is the supervised objective over the labeled dataset $\mathcal{C}$ (Eq. 4, page 3):
  $$L_2(\mathcal{C}) = \sum_{(x,y)} \log P(y \mid x^1, \ldots, x^m)$$
  where $P(y \mid x^1, \ldots, x^m) = \text{softmax}(h_l^m W_y)$ (Eq. 3, page 3).

- **$L_1(\mathcal{C})$** is the language modeling objective, used as an auxiliary objective and applied to $\mathcal{C}$. Its general form is Eq. 1 (page 3):
  $$L_1(\mathcal{U}) = \sum_i \log P(u_i \mid u_{i-k}, \ldots, u_{i-1}; \Theta)$$

- **$\lambda$** is the weight on the auxiliary objective. It was set to 0.5 (page 5).

The authors added the auxiliary language modeling objective because it improved generalization of the supervised model and sped up convergence (page 3). During fine-tuning, the only extra parameters are $W_y$ and the embeddings for delimiter tokens (page 3).
